- Primary goal: evaluate Redwood Inference for low-latency, cost-efficient LLM serving for Orion's customer-facing agents.
- Key constraints: SOC2 evidence + VPC deployment option, predictable p95 latency under 150ms for 512 tokens, and support for quantized weights.
- Stakeholders: Tom Hughes (CTO) for architecture and security, SRE team for performance validation, and procurement for SOW/terms.

We discussed a technical deep-dive / demo next to show: model routing, KV cache, and Dedicated capacity sizing. To move forward we typically do a VP/CTO alignment call (15–20 min) to unblock scheduling the full tech deep-dive with our solutions engineering team.

Attaching a one-page mutual action plan draft that outlines milestones so everyone sees the path to a pilot.

Marissa / Sean — confirmed. Tom will join the 10/22 15:00 PDT call and Maria (security) is on as well. I’ve accepted the invite and attached our internal architecture notes for context.

Quick answers to prep questions:
- Peak QPS (est): ~60–80 requests/sec during peak; median 18–22.
- Typical input token distribution: 64–256 tokens for most conversational requests; occasional long-form at ~1k tokens (~5% of traffic).
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II is required; encryption-at-rest and customer-managed keys are preferred.

Agenda looks good — for the tech deep-dive please include a short demo of prefix caching and how fallback routing to cheaper model variants would work during high load. We’ll also want to validate network egress and VPC peering approach.
